main.headline: the faster of Redux and Zustand
main.verdictRule: A tie is a difference in means within two standard errors. A larger difference is a win or a loss only if every browser restart agrees on the direction (the side that is faster in the pooled means is faster in each restart, restarts paired by restart number). Otherwise it is a tie.

scenarios.title: Selection
scenarios.description: Every row reads the selected id; 2 rows change

scenarios.title: Filter
scenarios.description: Every row derives whether it matches; half change

scenarios.title: Conditional read (inline)
scenarios.description: 1% of rows read a hot value in the row itself

scenarios.title: Conditional read (child component)
scenarios.description: 1% of rows read a hot value in a child that only mounts when expanded

scenarios.title: Subscribe churn
scenarios.description: Every 10th row's details mount, then unmount, so readers subscribe and unsubscribe

scenarios.title: Add / remove
scenarios.lowSignal: every variant does the same render work in the counting build, so it mostly measures list reconciliation, not store or selector work

comparisons.selectors: store + compiler vs the faster of Redux and Zustand
comparisons.zustand-granular: store + compiler vs the granular control (a Zustand store per entity)
comparisons.context-split: store + compiler vs a context per slice
comparisons.single-selectors: store-single (one store, no selectors) + compiler vs the faster of Redux and Zustand
comparisons.nocompiler-selectors: store without the compiler vs the faster of Redux and Zustand without the compiler
comparisons.compiler-gain: store + compiler vs store without the compiler
